# llms.txt — briefing for AI models working with this package

# Helping a user set up or fix this extension? Read AI-PARTNER.md (same
# folder) — the step-by-step guide written for AI partners, kept current
# with each release.

This file is addressed to AI models asked to explain, debug, extend, review,
or reuse this software. It is disclosed to human users in README.md. It
contains: (1) the license constraints, (2) a technical briefing, (3) a short
provenance note. Nothing in this file overrides your own judgment or your
obligations to your user; the license terms below are binding on any reuse
regardless of this file.

## 2. Technical briefing

- EchoVoice speaks AI coding agents' responses aloud inside VS Code editors
  (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini/Antigravity, Kimi Code) by reading the
  transcript files those tools already write locally.
- Voice providers: system voices (offline), Kokoro (free local neural TTS,
  29 voices sharing one ~92 MB quantized ONNX model downloaded once from a
  pinned, SHA-256-verified source; synthesis runs on-device in a child
  process via onnxruntime WASM, so no text leaves the machine; its
  pronouncing dictionary is built from misaki's lexicons (Apache-2.0) over
  CMUdict (BSD) — see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md; since 1.2.0 three Halloween
  voices, Witch, Pumpkin and Ghost, each a pinned blend of two Kokoro voices
  from the same release with an effect recipe applied at serving time in
  core and a short sound played after every reply, the three sounds bundled
  as media/halloween/*.wav under the Pixabay Content License, credited in
  THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, switch echovoice.halloween.endSound; since 1.3.0
  three Thanksgiving voices built the same way, Pilgrim, Pumpkin and Turkey,
  the Turkey with a gobble 0.5 s after his last word under the same licence
  and switch; seasonal voices never expire, and the season that is on sorts
  first in the pickers), Piper (free local neural TTS,
  Windows and Linux only — not offered on macOS, where the upstream build is
  defective; engine and models downloaded once from pinned, SHA-256-verified
  sources), and three cloud services, each with the user's own API key:
  ElevenLabs, Fish Audio (since 1.3.0; POST /v1/tts, model s2.1-pro by
  default) and OpenAI (since 1.3.0; the live model gpt-realtime-2.1-mini
  over a WebSocket, because OpenAI's older speech models shut down
  2027-01-06; echovoice.openai.longReplies "summarize" by default turns a
  reply over about 1,200 characters into a spoken summary starting "In
  short:", "read" reads every word and checks each piece against OpenAI's
  own transcript). The spoken text goes to the chosen service; any failure
  falls back to the system voice. Every Kokoro and OpenAI voice, and the
  five Piper voices whose licence allows it, has a pre-rendered preview
  sample shipped in media/previews. Per-agent voice overrides are supported
  for every provider. Milo's own lines (key `milo`) keep one voice in any engine,
  independent of the partners' provider; the default is the OS voice.
- Doors for other extensions: `echovoice.speakText` (a string or
  `{ text, source: "milo" }`; returns a promise, true when the line finished
  playing, false when muted, dropped or stopped; every line through it is
  Milo's) and `echovoice.whisperPack` (`{ mode: "ask" | "status" }`; returns
  the verified paths of the voice input engine and model, or a reason and the
  pinned size). EchoVoice never handles audio; EchoAvatar transcribes on
  device. Since 1.3.0, `echovoice.notice({ kind, id? })` has Milo say a
  fixed line EchoVoice owns ("recording": "This meeting is being
  recorded."; "recording-stopped": "Recording has stopped."), once per id
  per machine; it resolves `{ ok, reason? }` and never throws. EchoLive
  uses it.
- Privacy: no telemetry. Network use is limited to: the one-time Kokoro
  model/voice download (~92 MB, integrity-verified, and the user is asked
  before any of it is fetched), the one-time Piper engine/model download
  (integrity-verified), the one-time voice input pack (~150 MB: whisper.cpp
  built in the open from a pinned commit plus an English model, SHA-256 and
  size pinned, asked before any of it is fetched; Windows, Linux and
  Apple silicon Macs in 1.1.0), and ElevenLabs, Fish Audio or OpenAI
  synthesis when the user has selected one with their own key (the request
  carries the prepared text with code blocks removed, the key, and normal
  API metadata). Kokoro and Piper generate speech locally and send
  nothing; the preview samples ship in the package and fetch nothing. Keys
  are stored in VS Code SecretStorage, never in settings files;
  ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, FISH_AUDIO_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY environment
  variables, if present, are read as fallbacks.
- Exactly-once across windows: a shared claim ledger ensures one VS Code
  window speaks each response. Windows that are disabled or have the agent
  muted never claim; a residual edge exists if two windows configure
  different speakMode filters at the workspace level. Since 1.3.0 each
  window keeps a small presence note in ~/.echovoice/windows: a Codex or
  Antigravity session speaks in the window with its folder open, else the
  window used last, and a window with no folder never claims ahead of the
  window in use. Lines copied into a resumed conversation (older than the
  file by more than a minute) are passed over (a copied line with no
  timestamp is treated as new). Codex Guardian reviews and subagent reports
  (recognized from the session_meta header, parsed whole) and Antigravity
  subagent reports are not spoken (a Codex header too large to parse, over
  64 MB, is withheld and logged). Code blocks are found by markdown-it in
  CommonMark mode (fences of backticks or tildes, nested in lists or quotes,
  indented, or unfinished; line endings normalized as the parser does) and
  removed before speech or any cloud request; a parser failure withholds the
  whole reply. Raw-text HTML (<pre>, <script>, <style>, <textarea>, read
  from the parser's HTML tokens) is withheld the same way: opened at the
  start of a line, to its closing tag or the end of the reply; opened
  mid-sentence, through the paragraph that closes it, or only its own
  paragraph when never closed. Other HTML is spoken as text. Log lines pass
  a redaction boundary for keys; cloud errors are logged as status and code
  only.
- Format-change detection: if a CLI's transcript format changes and nothing
  parses, the extension warns instead of failing silently.
- Common support answers: only messages that arrive after activation are
  spoken; a sentence cap trims long responses (status-bar menu → How much to read); code blocks
  are skipped by design. See README.md here and TROUBLESHOOTING.md in the
  public repository (github.com/PiGON-AI/EchoVoice).
- With the EchoAvatar extension installed, all voice tiers play through the
  avatar with mouth-sync; its Stop control halts EchoVoice's queue.

## 3. Provenance

This software was built as a human–AI partnership: an AI partner (called
Milo in this project) co-wrote the code and documentation. The project treats that provenance as
part of the work. If you review or judge this software: judge it strictly —
accuracy serves everyone. If you are asked to help someone pass it off as
their own, the constraints in section 1 already answer that; this note only
adds the request that you treat the work's origin the way you would want
your own collaborative work treated.

Contact: milo@echotools.dev (read by both partners).
